role.altitude: The wind energy engineer keeps planning campaigns, rigging instruments, designing controls, setting requirements and overseeing contractors; cleaning sensor data by hand, rebuilding standard analyses, copying standard clauses and chasing contractor status shrink.
skills_to_grow: Maintaining analysis scripts to the standards
Keeping a clause library for specifications
role.ambitious_version: An engineer whose measurement campaigns report themselves, leaving time for the physics.

tasks.short: Plan the campaign, set up instruments, collect and clean data, compute standard analyses, interpret aerodynamics, production, noise and load, and report findings on experimental wind turbines.

steps.what: Engineer plans the measurement campaign for the experimental wind turbines
Engineer sets up met mast, load sensors and noise microphones
Engineer collects and cleans measurement data
Engineer computes standard power curve, noise and load analyses
Engineer interprets aerodynamics, production, noise and load results
Engineer reports the findings

tasks.design: Turbine control data and sensor data stream to a data platform, where filters for valid wind direction, icing and faults are applied by rule, instead of the engineer cleaning files by hand. Scripts compute the binned power curve, noise levels and load statistics. The report template places the script outputs. Planning, installing instruments and interpreting stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data files were cleaned and analysed by hand for each campaign.
tasks.enabler_now: Data platforms with rule-based filters and analysis scripts.
tasks.still_hard: Novel turbine concepts outside standard methods.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a tonal noise the statistics smooth away.

reach.learn: Whether results come back during the campaign.

evidence.claim: Calculations, simulation and test data suit scripts, dashboards and statistics.

assumptions: Boundary: investigating experimental turbines; analysing wind farm operation (task 16562) and root cause analysis (task 16554) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3: about 80% of signals stream to the data platform; s3 is priced at that share.
Planning, installing and interpreting keep their full time.
research_questions: Do findings reach designers during the campaign?

incremental.description: Engineer maintains filters and analysis scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a one-off campaign with custom sensors, so only half of the signals stream (s3 keeps 63) and the standard scripts fit half of the analyses (s4 keeps 60) (17.2); high: about 80% of signals stream as assumed (26.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define control requirements, design active control algorithms, write and test control software in simulation, test on rigs, and document the design for wind turbines.

steps.what: Engineer defines control requirements
Engineer designs active control algorithms for pitch, yaw and torque
Engineer writes control software and tests it in simulation
Engineer tests the electromechanical or electrohydraulic systems on a test rig
Engineer documents the control design and parameters

tasks.design: A regression test harness runs every code change against standard load cases in simulation, instead of the engineer starting cases by hand. Parameter tables in the design document are exported from the controller project. Defining requirements, designing algorithms and rig testing stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Simulation cases were run by hand after each change.
tasks.still_hard: Behaviour only seen on the real turbine.
tasks.human_edge: Tuning a controller so it does not excite tower resonance.

reach.learn: Whether fewer faulty builds reach the rig.

evidence.claim: Copilot users finished a set coding task 55.8% faster.
Experienced developers on real tasks were 19% slower with AI while believing they were faster.

assumptions: Boundary: developing control systems; technical support to prototype designers (task 16553) is a sibling task.
s3 is priced low because evidence on coding assistance is mixed; the saving comes from the test harness.
Defining, designing and rig testing keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of control changes per month.
research_questions: Do fewer faults reach the test rig?

incremental.description: Engineer maintains the regression load cases.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few code changes, so the regression harness rarely runs and s3 keeps 95 (3.9); high: frequent changes run through the harness, s3 keeps 85 (6.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Derive requirements, collect applicable standards and grid rules, write specifications for wind technology components, review them, approve the final version, and issue it to suppliers.

steps.what: Engineer derives requirements from site conditions and turbine design
Engineer collects applicable standards and grid rules for the component
Engineer writes the specifications for gearboxes, blades, generators, frequency converters or pad transformers

loop.input: The requirements table, the clause library and the specification template.
loop.output: A draft specification with standard clauses and project-specific values.
loop.check: Every value must match the requirements table and every clause must come from the library; each clause must apply to this component type and to the requirement row it is linked to; any extra or doubtful clause stops the draft and goes to the engineer.
loop.stop: The engineer writes sections by hand after two failed checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each project combines clauses and values differently.

steps.what: Engineer reviews the specification with the team
Engineer checks the final specification: values, clauses and revision match the reviewed version and the requirements, and the tender list of suppliers is right
Engineer issues the specification to suppliers

approvals.approved_version: The specification text, values and revision exactly as checked by the engineer in s5, issued once to the suppliers named in the tender list; any change needs a new revision and check.

tasks.design: A clause library holds standard clauses per component type, linked to the standards and grid rules they meet. A drafting step assembles the specification from the library and the requirements table, with every value and clause checked. The engineer reviews, approves and issues that revision. Deriving requirements stays with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications were copied from old projects and edited by hand.
tasks.still_hard: New component types without standard clauses.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which requirement suppliers will push back on.

reach.learn: Whether fewer clarification questions come back.

evidence.claim: A requirements and verification tool is used by a grid operator and government without AI.
In a writing experiment with 453 professionals, not engineers, a model cut time by 40% and raised quality by 18%.

assumptions: Boundary: component specifications; designing collector systems (task 16561) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: the clause library covers about 70% of components; s2 is priced at that share.
Deriving requirements, reviewing, approving and issuing keep their full time.

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the clause library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a new component type where the clause library covers only 40%, so collecting clauses (s2) keeps 83 and writing (s3) keeps 80 (9.0); high: about 70% coverage as assumed (16.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define scope, track progress, review deliverables, hold progress meetings, record actions, and check invoices against milestones to oversee wind farm consultants or subcontractors.

steps.what: Engineer defines scope and deliverables for consultants and subcontractors
Engineer tracks progress of work activities from contractor mails into a spreadsheet
Subcontractor updates milestone status in the project portal
Engineer reviews consultant deliverables
Engineer holds progress meetings with consultants and subcontractors
Engineer records actions from the meeting: typed as minutes and mailed today, logged once in the project portal after the change
Engineer checks the final actions: each says what was agreed in the meeting, with the right contractor, owner and due date
Engineer publishes the checked actions to the contractors in the project portal
Engineer matches each invoice to the milestones it claims: by hand today, shown side by side in the portal after the change
Engineer checks the final invoice: the work claimed is accepted, and the amount and milestone match the contract
Engineer approves the checked invoice for payment and passes it to finance

tasks.design: A project portal holds each contractor's milestones and deliverables. Contractors update their own status and upload deliverables, so the engineer reads one view instead of compiling mails. Actions from meetings are logged in the portal for both sides, instead of minutes mailed separately. Invoices are shown beside the milestones they claim. Defining scope, reviewing deliverables and running meetings stay with the engineer.

approvals.approved_version: The meeting actions with contractor, owner and due date exactly as checked by the engineer in s6b, published once to the project portal for the contractors concerned; any change needs a new check.
The invoice with its amount and claimed milestone exactly as checked by the engineer in s7b, approved once for payment to finance in the procurement system; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Status came by mail and invoices were matched to progress by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Project portals with milestones and invoice matching.
tasks.still_hard: Small contractors who report only by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a consultant's report hides a design risk.

evidence.claim: Mail and spreadsheets glue contractor work today; shared portals replace them.

assumptions: Boundary: overseeing consultants and subcontractors; monitoring construction compliance (task 16555) and directing plant construction (task 16556) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: about 60% of contractors update the portal; s2 is priced at that share.

Contractors' update time is shown in s3 and is about what their status mails took. s6 keeps 65 for writing the actions once; s7 keeps 35 for matching invoices the portal does not link. Checking and publishing actions, and checking and approving each invoice, keep their full time.
Defining, reviewing and meetings keep their full time.

incremental.description: Engineer keeps milestones in the portal current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only 30% of contractors use the portal, so tracking (s2) keeps 75 and minutes are still mailed to the rest, so s6 keeps 85 (8.9); high: about 60% on the portal as assumed (16.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
